text.en: This Order may be cited as the Legal Profession Act (Amendment) Order, 2003 and shall commence on the 1st. August, 2003. of long title.
The long title to the Legal Profession Act (Chapter 132), in this Order referred to as the Act, is amended by adding "Darussalam".

In this Order, unless the context otherwise requires - "Council" means the Council of the Society referred to in paragraph 10 of the "Society" means the Law Society of Brunei Darussalam established by His the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan in Council by an Order made under 62(1)fa). of Act.
The Act is amended by deleting the words "PART V PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE, CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE" where they appear immediately after section 22. of section 23 and saving.

{1) Subject to subsection (2}, section 23 of the Act is repealed.

(2) Any rules made by the Chief Justice, with the approval of His Majesty and Yang Di-Pertuan, under the repealed section 23 and in force immediately before the commencement of this Order shall, so far as they are not with the provisions of this Order, continue to be in force as if made 30th. 2003 that Order until they are amended or repealed by rules made by the Society with the approval of the Chief Justice. of section 24 and saving.

(1) Subject to subsection (2), section 24 of the Act is repealed.

(2) Any rules made by the Chief Justice, with the approval of His Majesty and Yang Di-Pertuan, under the repealed section 24 and in force immediately before the commencement of this Order shall, so far as they are not with the provisions of this Order, continue to be in force as if made under that Order until they are amended or repealed by rules made by the Society with the approval of the Chief Justice. of sections 25 to 28.
Sections 25, 26, 27 and 28 of the Act are repealed. of new sections 28A to 28E.

The Act is amended by inserting the following 5 new sections immediately "Qualification to use title of consultant. 28A. (1) and solicitor shall take or use the title of consultant unless he has, for a period of not less than 10 years in the aggregate, been either an advocate and solicitor in practice, a legal officer or both.

(2) and solicitor who contravenes subsection (1) is an offence and liable on conviction to a nne not exceeding $5,000. who are commissioners for oaths or notaries public. 28B. and solicitor who is a commissioner for oaths or a notary public shall do any act as such commissioner or notary public, as the case may be, unless he has in force a practising certificate. not to act as agent for unauthorised persons. 28C. (1) No advocate and solicitor shall(a) wilfully and knowingly act as agent for any unauthorised person in any legal proceedings of whatsoever kind or in any matter Act can be done only by an advocate and solicitor who has in force a practising certificate; {b J permit his name to be made use of in any such proceedings or matter upon the account or for the profi.t of any unauthorised {c} send any process to any unauthorised person, or do any other act enabling any unauthorised person to appear, act or practise or to practise in any respect as an advocate and solicitor in any such proceedings or matter.

(2) and solicitor shall authorise any unauthorised person bank account in the name of the advocate and solicitor or his fi.rm and maintained by the advocate and solicitor or his fi.rm in connection with his practice as an advocate and solicitor.

(3) Disciplinary proceedings may be taken against any advocate and who acts in contravention of subsection (1) or (2).

(4) Any unauthorised person who was enabled by an advocate and or practise or purport to practise as an advocate and solicitor an offence and liable on conviction to a fi.ne not exceeding $2,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months.

(5) In this section, "unauthorised person" has the meaning assigned to it in subsection (1) of section 18. by advocate and solicitor. 28D. ( 1) th,e relationship of advocate and solicitor and client exists, or has existed, a summons may be issued by the client or his representative for the delivery of a cash account, the payment of moneys or for the delivery of securities.

(2) A Judge may order the respondent to deliver to the applicant a list of the moneys or securities yvhich he has in his custody or control on behalf of the applicant, or to bring the whole or any part of it into court, within such time as the Judge orders.

(3) In the event of the respondent alleging that he has a claim for costs, the Judge may make such provision for the payment or security thereof or for the protection of the respondent's lien, if any, as he thinks fi.t. of Council to inspect tiles of proceedings in bankruptcy of advocate and solicitor. 28E. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other written law, the Council may, without payment of any fee, inspect the tiles of proceedings in relating to any advocate and solicitor against whom proceedings in bankruptcy have been taken, and shall be entitled to be supplied with or certified copies of those proceedings on payment of the usual charges for those copies.". of Part VI.

Part VI of the Act is repealed: that this section shall not have effect in relation to any proceedings the repealed section 29 to show cause which were pending on the date of of this Order. Further amendment of Act.
Part VIII of the Act is amended, in the sub-heading immediately below "MISCELLANEOUS AND GENERAL", by adding "Darussalam". of section 62.
Section 62 of the Act is amended, in paragraph {a) of subsection (1), by adding of section 63.
Section 63 of the Act is amended by inserting "Darussalam" immediately after "Brunei" in the first line. of section 64.

Section 64 of the Act is amended by inserting "or in pursuance of rules made by the Society with the approval of the Chief Justice under the powers conferred on it by the First Schedule" immediately after "23" in the second line. of section 65.
Section 65 of the Act is amended, in subsection (2), by deleting paragraph {a). of First Schedule.

The First Schedule to the Act is amended - fa} in the fi.rst heading, by adding 11Darussalam"; {b) by deleting "bye-laws" from(i) the third line of paragraph 1; (iiJ the third line of paragraph 8; and

(iii) the third line of paragraph 19, and by substituting "rules" therefor; {c) by adding the following new paragraphs"21. With the approval of the Chief Justice, provision for the Society to make rules for the regulation of professional practice, etiquette, conduct and discipline of advocates and solicitors.
With the approval of the Chief Justice, provision for the Society to make rules for the opening and closing and keeping by advocates and solicitors of accounts at banks for clients money.
With the approval of the Chief Justice, provision for the Society to an accountant's report to be delivered with every application for a practising certificate.
With the approval of the Chief Justice, provision for the Society to make rules co:ticerning indemnity against loss arising from claims an advocate and solicitor in respect of civil liability.
Circumstances in which the Society can exercise powers in respect of inadequate professional services by an advocate and solicitor.
Power to limit pn;,fessional experience before practising on own account or in partnership.
Regulation of the employment and remuneration of employees.

Circumstances in which the Society has power to intervene in an and solicitor's practice.". 30th. JULY, 2003 of Jamadilawal, 1424 Hijriah corresponding to the 1st. day of July, 2003 at Our Istana Nurul Iman, Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei
